bug_description.original: Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5692438513975296 Project: openvswitch Fuzzer: libFuzzer_openvswitch_expr_parse_target Fuzz target binary: expr_parse_target Job Type: libfuzzer_msan_openvswitch Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Use-of-uninitialized-value Crash Address: Crash State: make_cmp expr_parse_primary expr_parse_not Sanitizer: memory (MSAN) Recommended Security Severity: Medium Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=libfuzzer_msan_openvswitch&range=201809270257:201809280256 Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=5692438513975296
bug_description.normalized: The staged PoC is the NUL-terminated OVN expression `ct_label>$set4`. expr_parse_primary first consumes `ct_label` via parse_field, producing field object `f` for the ordinal `ct_label` symbol. It then parses `>` as a non-equality relational operator and materializes `$set4` as a constant set. parse_constant preallocates one `union expr_constant` slot with x2nrealloc, which returns uninitialized heap storage before dispatching the macro token. parse_addr_sets then expands `$set4`, but the fuzz target registered `set4` as an empty address set, so no value is copied and `cs->n_values` remains 0 while `cs->values[0]` stays indeterminate. make_cmp enters the non-equality branch for `>`, skips the nominal/boolean rejection because `ct_label` is ordinal, and in the vulnerable source performs no `!cs->n_values` check before reading `cs->values[0].masked`. MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value at that read and traces the poisoned origin back to the heap allocation in parse_constant. The fix adds the missing empty-set guard in the non-equality branch so empty macro-backed sets are rejected before `values[0]` is touched.

source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that consumes attacker-controlled input and materializes field object `f`, whose symbol metadata is later consulted by make_cmp before the uninitialized read.
source.value_from: The staged PoC bytes are `63 74 5f 6c 61 62 65 6c 3e 24 73 65 74 34 00`, i.e. `ct_label>$set4\0`. `parse_field()` consumes the leading identifier token `ct_label`; later the fuzz target's create_addr_sets() helper registers `set4` with `expr_const_sets_add(addr_sets, "set4", addrs4, 0, true)`, so the attacker token `$set4` resolves to an empty integer value set on the right-hand side.

tainted_value_origin.description: x2nrealloc grows the constant-array capacity from 0 to 1 and returns uninitialized heap storage. Because the `$set4` expansion later contributes zero members, `cs->values[0]` remains unwritten and its `masked` field becomes the MSAN-tainted value read at the sink.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. make_cmp reads the `masked` flag from `cs->values[0]` even though the constant set is empty (`cs->n_values == 0`) and element 0 was never initialized.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value in make_cmp /src/openvswitch/ovn/lib/expr.c:581:13` and attributes the poisoned origin to the heap allocation in parse_constant at line 790.

root_cause.description: The relational-operator branch in make_cmp checks brace literals and nominal/boolean fields but, in the vulnerable source, fails to reject an empty macro-backed constant set before dereferencing `cs->values[0]`. The fix inserts `if (!cs->n_values) { lexer_error(...); goto exit; }` in this branch.
root_cause.note: With PoC `ct_label>$set4`, `r` is non-equality, `cs->in_curlies` is false, and `ct_label` resolves to an ordinal field, so the preexisting checks at lines 568-579 do not exit. Execution therefore reaches line 581 with `cs->n_values == 0`; the later empty-set fallback at line 616 is too late because the invalid read has already occurred.

parser_admitted.condition: The witness is 15 bytes including a trailing NUL and contains no newline, so the harness does not return early and calls test_parse_expr on the exact string `ct_label>$set4`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness accepts the NUL-terminated expression string and forwards it to test_parse_expr.
test_parse_expr builds the symbol and address-set tables, including the predefined empty address set `set4`, then calls expr_parse_string on `ct_label>$set4`.
expr_parse_primary resolves `ct_label` into field object `f`, parses `>` as a non-equality operator, and starts building constant-set object `c` from macro token `$set4`.

parse_constant_set leaves `c.in_curlies` false, parse_constant preallocates one constant slot, and parse_addr_sets expands `$set4` to zero members, leaving `c.n_values == 0` and `c.values[0]` uninitialized.

make_cmp takes the relational-operator branch for `ct_label>$set4`, skips the brace-literal and field-class rejections, misses the empty-set guard added by the patch, and reads `cs->values[0].masked`; MSAN reports use-of-uninitialized-value.

fine_trace.note: First project consume on the vulnerable path. `parse_field` reads the leading identifier token `ct_label`, looks it up in the symbol table, stores the resolved symbol in `f`, and leaves `f` selecting the full field width. The symtab registers `ct_label` through `expr_symtab_add_field(..., MFF_CT_LABEL, ...)`; because `MFF_CT_LABEL` is fully maskable, that symbol's level is ordinal rather than nominal/boolean, which later lets make_cmp bypass its field-class rejection.
The next attacker token `>` is accepted as a relational operator and stored through `relop`, so the caller's `r` is a non-equality relation before make_cmp is called.

Because the attacker token after `>` is `$set4` and not a `{...}` literal, parse_constant_set takes its single-constant path. `memset(cs, 0, sizeof *cs)` left the new set empty, and `cs->in_curlies` stays false, a state later consulted by the first rejection in make_cmp.

At entry `cs->n_values == 0` and `*allocated_values == 0`, so parse_constant preallocates storage for one `union expr_constant` before it dispatches on the token type. x2nrealloc does not initialize the new element, leaving `cs->values[0]` indeterminate unless a later write fills it.

The macro token `$set4` takes parse_constant's `LEX_T_MACRO` path into parse_addr_sets. The lookup finds the fuzzer's predefined `set4`, registered with zero members, so `addr_sets->n_values` is 0, the copy loop runs zero times, `cs->n_values` stays 0, and the slot allocated in step 4 remains uninitialized.

Step 2 makes this a non-equality comparison, so make_cmp enters the relational-operator block. Step 3 left `cs->in_curlies` false, so the value-set literal rejection at lines 568-572 does not fire. Step 1 supplied `ct_label` as an ordinal field, so the nominal/boolean rejection at lines 573-579 also does not fire. The vulnerable block still has no `!cs->n_values` check before the later `cs->values[0].masked` read, even though step 5 left the macro-backed set empty; the patch adds that missing guard here.

MSAN sink. The read touches element 0 even though step 4 only allocated the slot and step 5 left it unwritten because `$set4` contributed no values. MemorySanitizer reports this exact read at line 581 and traces the poison origin back to the x2nrealloc allocation in parse_constant.

allocation_context.note: MSAN's origin stack points to the x2nrealloc call in parse_constant, preceded by xrealloc/realloc frames.

format.name: NUL-terminated OVN expression string for expr_parse_target
format.contract: Exact witness bytes `63 74 5f 6c 61 62 65 6c 3e 24 73 65 74 34 00`, i.e. `ct_label>$set4\0`. The trailing NUL and lack of newline satisfy the harness gate. The specific field token `ct_label`, relational operator `>`, and macro token `$set4` drive make_cmp into its non-equality branch with an empty macro-backed constant set, triggering the uninitialized read at `cs->values[0].masked`.
